many theories were put forward in June as to the nature of how the voat exodus would play out. among the possibilities were sabotage by reddit and collapse, massive support and the new front page of the internet, or just a soft whimper and back to obscurity.

with 3 months now down the line we can look back and see the shape of not only Voat, but reddits reaction to it. here are my conclusions:

1- reddit staff did a very smart thing by finally simply shutting up about the Pao controversy, suppressing dissent, and hiding negative content. 99% of reddit users give 0 shits about the politics of the internet and just want content. reddit kept giving them that content throughout these months.

2- the new Voat community did a very stupid thing by making their front page entirely self referential. most of Voats early top page content was... well about voat or about reddit or about closely associated "free speech" topics. nothing to hold a general "reddit type" audience and nothing (at first) to draw in special interest groups.

3- in the vaccum of content that is and was the Voat front page, two things occurred. first, and the most obvious, are the reposts. the Voat front page is roughly 45% directly reposted content from reddits front page. the amount of total reposts from other reddit subs is simply too high for me to properly quantify. simply put, the odds of content existing on Voat but NOT existing on reddit is very, very low. the second shift of front page content occurred within just a few weeks of the exodus. i wont belabor you with social theories or half baked explanations as to why... but for some reason, the community at Voat is more inclined to post and upvote things that sane humans would characterize as racism and sexism. now sexism might be too complicated of a concept to apply to the voat community. it could be better described as a simple FEAR of women.

so that leaves us with an aggregate of reposted "general" content (the dog gifs, world news, bernie quotes, and techno talk that hit reddit's front page 3 hours ago), original self referential content (voat site news, Pao hate, reddit hate, and related internet censorship news including things quasi banned on reddit like TPP talk), and what i like to call the "SJW posts" (mens rights conspiracies, blatant and veiled racism, female hate/fear posts, fattie hate posts, and all the "scary news" fear-monger type crap that networks like Fox News run on the reg) I call these SJW posts for two reasons. One, its the insult of choice on Voat. And two, its actually a great description of the majority of people throwing it around. they just want a different kind of "social justice". they are still just as whinny, ineffectual, entitled, and sensitive as the "real" SJWs they hate.

the end result? i check voat about once a week, maybe less, just to see whats new and see what reddit has kept hidden for the week. i stopped posting new and even rehashed content because i dont think the community is worth my time. i think other... "normal" users are starting to feel the same way.

so what was the Voat exodus? in real terms, not in any political context? it was the moving of a (frankly undesirable) community to a site that will now hopefully cater to their tastes and keep them from polluting reddit. in this sense, Voat was wildly successful and reddit users should consider this model for getting other "unsavory types" to leave of their own accord.
